html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Explain the network model and the role of CNI plugins
  • Choose a Service type and trace how DNS and kube-proxy deliver traffic
  • Route outside traffic with Ingress and Gateway API
  • Restrict traffic with a NetworkPolicy, and recognize a service mesh

2The Kubernetes network model, who assigns addresses, CNI and plugin examples

Running case

Harbor Books Connects Its Parts

  • The storefront, catalog, orders and postgres Pods must find each other, even as Pods are replaced
  • Each part needs a stable address, and visitors need a route from the internet to the storefront
  • Only orders may call postgres; every other Pod must be kept out
  • In this module you build the network around the shop

The Kubernetes Network Model

  • Every Pod gets its own unique IP address, valid across the whole cluster
  • Containers in one Pod share a network namespace and reach each other on localhost
  • Any Pod can reach any other Pod directly, with no proxy and no NAT (network address translation)
  • Agents on a node, such as the kubelet, can reach all Pods on that node

Exam tip: Pod IPs come from the network plugin, Service IPs from the API server.

CNI and Network Plugins Beyond the curriculum

Plugin What it is known for
Cilium an eBPF-based dataplane for networking, observability and security; enforces network policy up to the application layer
Calico a CNI network plugin with Kubernetes network policy support
Flannel a simple layer 3 network fabric; the flanneld agent gives each host a subnet
  • A CNI plugin (Container Network Interface) implements the network model: it gives Pods their addresses and connects them
  • A cluster needs a CNI plugin; the choice changes features such as NetworkPolicy support

Exam tip: A CNI plugin builds the Pod network, and policy enforcement depends on the plugin.

3Services and their types, EndpointSlices and kube-proxy, DNS and service discovery, CoreDNS, what the exam asks

Services: A Stable Address for Pods

  • Pods are replaced often, and each replacement has a new IP
  • A Service gives a set of Pods one stable name and virtual IP
  • A label selector chooses which Pods belong to the Service
  • Clients call the Service, and Kubernetes load balances the traffic over the matching Pods

Exam tip: A Service finds its Pods by labels, not by names.

Service Types

Type What it does
ClusterIP (default) a virtual IP inside the cluster, reachable only from within it
NodePort opens the same port on every node, from 30000-32767 by default, on top of a ClusterIP
LoadBalancer uses an external load balancer, which Kubernetes does not provide itself; a cloud provider usually does
ExternalName answers with a CNAME (alias record) for an outside DNS name; no proxying
Headless clusterIP: None: no virtual IP, and DNS returns the Pod IPs

Exam tip: ClusterIP is the default; NodePort and LoadBalancer expose a Service outside.

A Service Manifest

  • A Service picks its Pods with a selector on their labels
  • port is the port clients call; targetPort is the port in the container
  • If you leave out targetPort, it is the same as port
  • type defaults to ClusterIP

A Service for the catalog Pods

apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: catalog
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: catalog
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 8080

Exam tip: port is what clients call; targetPort is where the container listens.

EndpointSlices and kube-proxy

  • For a Service with a selector, Kubernetes creates EndpointSlices automatically; they list the matching Pods' addresses
  • A slice holds at most 100 endpoints by default, so a big Service has several slices
  • The older Endpoints API is deprecated
  • kube-proxy runs on each node and sets up the rules that send Service traffic to those addresses, in iptables, ipvs or nftables mode on Linux

Exam tip: The Service is the name, the EndpointSlice is the list, kube-proxy is the plumbing.

DNS, CoreDNS and Service Discovery

  • Pods find a Service in two ways: DNS and environment variables
  • The kubelet adds {SVCNAME}_SERVICE_HOST and {SVCNAME}_SERVICE_PORT to new Pods, so the Service must exist before the Pod
  • DNS has no ordering problem; the full name joins the Service name, the namespace, svc and the cluster domain
  • CoreDNS, a CNCF graduated project, is the cluster DNS add-on

Exam tip: Same namespace: short name. Other namespace: name.namespace.

What the Exam Asks: Networking

  • Pod IP or Service IP: a Pod has its own IP from the network plugin; a Service gives a stable virtual IP
  • ClusterIP, NodePort or LoadBalancer: inside only, a port on every node, or an external load balancer
  • Service or Ingress: a Service exposes Pods; an Ingress routes HTTP by host and path to Services
  • Ingress or Gateway API: Gateway API is the successor; both need a controller or implementation
  • kube-proxy or CoreDNS: kube-proxy sets up forwarding rules; CoreDNS answers names
  • NetworkPolicy: open by default, additive, and needs a plugin that enforces it

Exam tip: For a networking question, name the layer first: address, name, route or rule.

4Ingress, Gateway API, the Ingress NGINX retirement, MetalLB

Ingress: HTTP Routes into the Cluster

  • Ingress routes HTTP and HTTPS traffic from outside the cluster to Services, using rules on host and path
  • An Ingress is only rules: an Ingress controller must be running to act on them
  • ingressClassName says which controller handles an Ingress
  • The Ingress API is frozen: it stays and is stable, but gets no new features

Exam tip: No Ingress controller, no routing.

Gateway API and the Ingress NGINX Retirement Moving

Kind Role
GatewayClass a set of gateways with common configuration, run by one controller
Gateway the entry point that actually takes in traffic, for example a cloud load balancer
HTTPRoute HTTP rules that map traffic from a Gateway to backends, often Services
GRPCRoute the same for gRPC traffic
  • Gateway API is the successor to Ingress: an add-on that is role-oriented, portable, expressive and extensible
  • As of 30 October 2026: the Ingress NGINX controller was retired in March 2026, with no more releases, bug fixes or security updates; existing installations keep working
  • The project advises moving to Gateway API or another Ingress controller

Exam tip: Gateway API replaces Ingress for new designs; a retired controller still runs but gets no fixes.

LoadBalancer Without a Cloud: MetalLB Beyond the curriculum

Where the cluster runs Who creates the load balancer
A cloud provider the provider's load balancer integration
Your own hardware (bare metal) an add-on such as MetalLB
  • A Service of type LoadBalancer needs an external load balancer, and Kubernetes does not provide one itself
  • MetalLB fills that gap for bare-metal clusters, with an implementation built on standard routing protocols

Exam tip: LoadBalancer needs something to make the load balancer: a cloud, or MetalLB on bare metal.

5NetworkPolicy

NetworkPolicy: Rules for Pod Traffic

  • By default Pods are non-isolated: all inbound and outbound traffic is allowed
  • A policy that selects a Pod makes it isolated for that direction; only allowed traffic gets through
  • Policies are additive: they never conflict, and the allowed traffic is the union of their rules
  • Rules select peers with podSelector, namespaceSelector or ipBlock
  • The network plugin enforces policies; without support a policy has no effect

Only orders Pods may reach postgres

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: postgres-from-orders
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels: {app: postgres}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels: {app: orders}

Exam tip: Open by default; once a policy selects a Pod, only what policies allow gets in.

6Service mesh, sidecar and sidecarless

Service Mesh: Sidecar and Sidecarless Archived topic

  • A service mesh manages traffic between services and adds reliability, observability and security the same way for all of them, without code changes
  • Sidecar design: a proxy beside each app intercepts its traffic and enforces policy, at the cost of more resources
  • Sidecarless design: the work moves out of the Pods, for example into the kernel with eBPF
  • Examples: Istio (Envoy sidecars, plus an ambient mode) and Linkerd; a common feature is mutual TLS (mTLS)

Exam tip: A mesh handles traffic between services; Ingress and Gateway API handle traffic coming in.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which statement describes the Kubernetes network model?

  • APods on different nodes can reach one another through a NodePort Service
  • BEach node hands its Pods private addresses, and traffic between nodes is translated by NAT
  • CEach Pod has its own cluster-wide IP, and Pods talk to each other directly without NAT
  • DThe containers in the cluster share one network namespace and a single IP address
Show the answer

Answer: C. Every Pod gets its own unique IP, valid across the cluster, and Pods communicate directly without proxies or NAT. Only the containers of one Pod share a network namespace.

S2The Harbor Books storefront must call the catalog Pods, which are replaced often and get new IPs each time. What gives the storefront a stable address to call?

  • AA Service whose selector matches the labels of the catalog Pods
  • BA ConfigMap that holds the current IP addresses of the catalog Pods, updated by hand
  • CA NodePort opened on the node where the first catalog Pod happens to be running
  • DA DaemonSet that restarts the storefront Pods every time a catalog Pod changes
Show the answer

Answer: A. A Service gives the Pods that match its selector one stable name and virtual IP, however often individual Pods change. A ConfigMap would need manual updates, a NodePort points at one node, and restarting the storefront does not give it an address.

S3Which Service type uses an external load balancer, for example one from a cloud provider?

  • AClusterIP, which exposes the Service on a virtual IP that is reachable from inside the cluster
  • BExternalName, which answers with a CNAME record for a DNS name outside the cluster
  • CHeadless, which has no virtual IP and returns the addresses of the Pods from DNS
  • DLoadBalancer, which uses an external load balancer for access from outside
Show the answer

Answer: D. The LoadBalancer type exposes a Service through an external load balancer, which Kubernetes does not provide itself; a cloud provider usually does. ClusterIP stays inside the cluster, ExternalName only maps a name, and a headless Service has no virtual IP.

S4A storefront Pod in the namespace shop must call the Service orders in the namespace backend. Which name does it use?

  • Aorders, because a short name resolves in the other namespaces of the cluster
  • Borders.backend, because the namespace follows the Service name
  • Cbackend.orders, because the namespace comes before the Service name
  • Dorders.shop, because a Pod searches its own namespace first for each name
Show the answer

Answer: B. The short name only works for a Service in the Pod's own namespace. For another namespace the name is the Service name followed by the namespace, here orders.backend, or the full form orders.backend.svc.cluster.local.

S5Harbor Books created an Ingress with host and path rules for the storefront, but no traffic reaches the Pods. What is a likely cause?

  • AThe Ingress must be created in the kube-system namespace to have any effect on traffic
  • BNo Ingress controller is running, and an Ingress resource alone has no effect
  • CThe Ingress API was removed from Kubernetes, so the resource is simply ignored
  • DIngress rules can match the host of a request, but never the path of a request
Show the answer

Answer: B. An Ingress is only a set of rules, and an Ingress controller must be running to act on them. The Ingress API is frozen but not removed, it can be created in any namespace, and rules can match both host and path.

S6Which statement about Gateway API and Ingress is correct?

  • AGateway API replaces Services, so a cluster that uses it does not need Service objects
  • BIngress was removed from Kubernetes, so Gateway API is the way to route HTTP traffic
  • CThe two are the same API, and the names of their kinds differ between them
  • DGateway API is the successor to Ingress, with kinds such as GatewayClass, Gateway and HTTPRoute
Show the answer

Answer: D. Gateway API is the successor to Ingress and is role-oriented, with kinds such as GatewayClass, Gateway and HTTPRoute. Routes usually point at Services, and the Ingress API is frozen but still available.

S7A namespace has no NetworkPolicy. Which traffic is allowed to and from its Pods?

  • AAll ingress and egress traffic, because Pods are non-isolated by default
  • BNo traffic at all, until the first policy is created to allow some of it
  • COnly the traffic that stays inside the namespace, because policies are scoped to it
  • DOnly egress traffic, because ingress stays blocked until a rule opens it
Show the answer

Answer: A. Pods are non-isolated by default, so with no policy all inbound and outbound traffic is allowed. A Pod becomes isolated for a direction only when a policy selects it.

S8Harbor Books applies a NetworkPolicy that lets only the orders Pods reach postgres, yet other Pods still connect. Which cause is most likely?

  • ANetworkPolicy objects apply to Pods that belong to a StatefulSet
  • BThe same policy also needs to be created for the orders Pods before it takes effect
  • CThe network plugin of the cluster does not enforce NetworkPolicy
  • DA second policy in the namespace overrides the first one and reopens the traffic
Show the answer

Answer: C. The network plugin does the enforcing, and a policy without a plugin that supports it has no effect. Policies apply to any selected Pods, need no matching policy on the callers, and are additive rather than overriding.

S9What does a service mesh provide for the services of a cluster?

  • AReliability, observability and security features, applied the same way to all services without code changes
  • BPersistent storage that several Pods on different nodes can share at the same time
  • CA place to build container images and push them to a registry from inside the cluster
  • DThe scheduling of Pods onto nodes according to the requests of their containers
Show the answer

Answer: A. A service mesh manages the traffic between services and adds reliability, observability and security uniformly, usually with proxies, without changes to application code. Storage, image builds and scheduling belong to other parts of the platform.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Network model one IP per Pod, direct Pod-to-Pod traffic with no NAT; a CNI plugin builds it
Services a stable name and virtual IP over a label-selected set of Pods; ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, ExternalName, headless
Behind a Service EndpointSlices list the Pods, kube-proxy programs the rules, CoreDNS answers the names
From outside Ingress needs a controller; Gateway API is the successor; MetalLB serves bare metal
NetworkPolicy open by default, additive, enforced by the plugin
Service mesh sidecar or sidecarless proxies add security, reliability and observability
